simple.meaning: שְׁרֵקָה (shᵉrêqâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a derision.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 8 times across 2 Chronicles, Jeremiah, Micah, beginning at 2 Chronicles 29:8. Its contexts include kingship, city, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שְׁרֵקָה (H8322).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שְׁרֵקָה (shᵉrêqâh) / H8322 is traced through 2 Chronicles 29:8, Jeremiah 18:16, Jeremiah 19:8, Jeremiah 25:9 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H8322. shereqah שְׁרֵקָה noun feminine (object of derisive) hissing ; — always absolute ׳שׁ , and always + שַׁמָּה : Jer 19:3 ; 25:9 , 18 (+ פְלָלָה חָרְבָּה, ), 29:18 (+ חֶרְמָּה אָלָה, ), 51:27 ; Micah 6:16 (+ חֶרְמָּה ), 2Chr 29:8 .

occurrences.englishText: Therefore Yahweh’s wrath was on Judah and Jerusalem, and he has delivered them to be tossed back and forth, to be an astonishment, and a hissing, as you see with your eyes.
to make their land an astonishment,
I will make this city an astonishment and a hissing. Everyone who passes by it will be astonished and hiss because of all its plagues.

behold, I will send and take all the families of the north,” says Yahweh, “and I will send to Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will bring them against this land, and against its inhabitants, and against all these nations around. I will utterly destroy them, and make them an astonishment, and a hissing, and perpetual desolations.
Jerusalem, and the cities of Judah, with its kings and its princes, to make them a desolation, an astonishment, a hissing, and a curse, as it is today;

I will pursue after them with the sword, with the famine, and with the pestilence, and will deliver them to be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth, to be an object of horror, an astonishment, a hissing, and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them,
For the statutes of Omri are kept,
